# 📄 Introduce Yourself

## 🎯 Overview

Introduce yourself to the class with a **GitHub profile README**: a short bio, written in
Markdown, that appears at the top of your GitHub profile at
`https://github.com/<your-username>`.

Your profile is the start of your online presence. Over the term, you'll pin your best work
to it, so by the end it works as a small portfolio you can keep building in later courses.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This assignment works differently from the rest of the course. Your repo must be named
> **exactly** your GitHub username, and you work on `main`. There's no `develop` branch, no
> pull request, and no GitHub Pages site.

## 📋 Requirements

- [ ] You created your own repo from this template, owned by your GitHub account
- [ ] The repo is named **exactly** your GitHub username, like `daveberning/daveberning`
- [ ] The repo is **Public**
- [ ] `README.md` introduces you in your own words: who you are, and what you hope to get out
      of this course
- [ ] Your introduction uses Markdown: at least one heading, one list, and one link. Any
      image has alt text that describes it.
- [ ] Your changes are committed and pushed to `main`
- [ ] Your introduction shows at the top of your profile at `https://github.com/<your-username>`
- [ ] You took the screenshots listed on the assignment page in Canvas, and submitted them there

## 🛠️ Steps

1. **Create your repo from this template.** Click **Use this template** → **Create a new
   repository**. Set **Owner** to your GitHub account, name it **exactly** your GitHub
   username, set it to **Public**, and click **Create repository**. GitHub shows a note
   that this is a special repo; that's how you know the name is right.
2. **Clone it in WebStorm.** Follow step 2 of the [Getting Started guide](GETTING_STARTED.md).
   Skip step 3: stay on `main`.
3. **Write your introduction** in `README.md`, below the comment at the top. Use the
   [Markdown cheat sheet](../CHEATSHEET.md) for headings, lists, links, and images. WebStorm
   shows a live preview next to the file.
4. **Commit and push to `main`.** Press <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>, check your files,
   write a message, and click **Commit**. Then press <kbd>Cmd</kbd> +
   <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> and click **Push**. The
   [Publishing guide](PUBLISHING.md) has screenshots of both. Ignore its GitHub Pages steps.
5. **Check your profile** at `https://github.com/<your-username>`. Your introduction should
   be at the top.

## 📂 Starter Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | Your introduction. It starts with a comment that won't show on your profile. |
| `CHEATSHEET.md` | Markdown examples to copy from. It won't show on your profile. |

To add a photo, put the image file in the root of the repo next to `README.md` and link it
with a relative path, like `![A short description of the photo](me.jpg)`.

> [!CAUTION]
> Your profile is public. Use a photo you're comfortable sharing, and leave out anything you
> don't want online, like your address or phone number.

## 🧮 Grading

| Criteria | What earns full credit | Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Repo setup** | Created from this template, owned by your account, named exactly your GitHub username, and Public. | 1 |
| **Introduction** | `README.md` introduces you in your own words: who you are, and what you hope to get out of this course. | 2 |
| **Markdown** | Uses at least one heading, one list, and one link, all rendering correctly on your profile. Any image loads and has descriptive alt text. | 1 |
| **Published and submitted** | Your changes are pushed to `main`, the introduction shows on your profile, and the screenshots are submitted in Canvas. | 1 |
| **Total** |  | **5** |

## 🤖 AI Policy

Work on this assignment must be your own. Do not use AI tools — including GitHub Copilot,
Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, or JetBrains AI Assistant — to write your introduction.

This repo includes a `.noai` file, which disables JetBrains AI Assistant for the project
in IDEs like WebStorm. Leave it in place. It is a reminder of the policy above, not a
substitute for it — following the policy is still your responsibility.
